body:
Wendy's said on Thursday it had rejected a $1.4 billion take-private offer from activist investor Nelson Peltz's Trian Fund Management and its partners, resisting pressure from one of its largest shareholders.

The food chain also adopted a "poison pill" plan, known as a limited-duration shareholder rights plan, which aims to stop investors from amassing more than 15% of the company.

Trian and related parties own a 16.3% stake in Wendy's, according to a regulatory filing.

Peltz was partnering with restaurant operator Flynn Group and investment firms BlueFive Capital and Sixth Street Partners on the proposed acquisition, looking to revive the US fast-food chain's struggling sales away from the glare of public-market investors.

"The proposal substantially undervalues the company," the independent board committee created to evaluate the offer said.

Trian, which considered taking Wendy's private in 2022, backed away in 2023. It has campaigned to change strategy and board composition at various companies including Walt Disney, Kraft Heinz and Procter & Gamble.

The activist investor declined to comment.

In recent years, buyout firms have tried to purchase other publicly traded restaurants, including Papa John's, which has fended off offers from Irth Capital and Apollo Global over the last year.
